MATHEMATICALThe trace-moment argument
Definitions · lemmas · proof

A short formalization of the moment method, with the analytic and combinatorial inputs isolated as lemmas.

00
The setting

A symmetric sign matrix

We study a real symmetric matrix with zero diagonal and independent uniform signs above the diagonal.The source is released under Apache 2.0 by the random-matrices-lean contributors.The Lean file uses Mathlib’s probability measure on binomial random graphs, its adjacency-matrix API, and the standard ℓ2\ell^2ℓ2 operator norm.Throughout, it opens the usual measure, operator-norm, and unit-interval notation.All declarations lie in RandomMatrices.IndependentRademacher.

For a simple graph GGG on {0,…,n−1}\{0,\ldots,n-1\}{0,…,n−1}, define the signed adjacency matrix

M(G)=2A(G)−A(Kn).M(G)=2A(G)-A(K_n).M(G)=2A(G)−A(Kn​).

Thus Mii=0M_{ii}=0Mii​=0, while Mij=1M_{ij}=1Mij​=1 on an edge and Mij=−1M_{ij}=-1Mij​=−1 on a non-edge.Sampling G∼G(n,12)G\sim G(n,\tfrac12)G∼G(n,21​) makes these off-diagonal signs independent and symmetric.The definition symmetricRademacherMeasure is precisely this graph law.

01
Definitions

The walks which survive

A closed walk of length ℓ\ellℓ is represented by a function w:Fin⁡(ℓ)→Fin⁡(n)w:\operatorname{Fin}(\ell)\to\operatorname{Fin}(n)w:Fin(ℓ)→Fin(n).The cyclic permutation finRotate sends each time to the next time and the last time back to zero.

At time ttt, the walk crosses the unordered edge {w(t),w(t+1)}\{w(t),w(t+1)\}{w(t),w(t+1)}, represented by Mathlib’s Sym2.The multiplicity me(w)m_e(w)me​(w) is the number of times that edge eee occurs.

Double coverage
A walk is double-covered when it has no stationary step and every edge multiplicity is even.Unused edges have multiplicity zero, which is even.
w(t)≠w(t+1),me(w)≡0(mod2)for every e.w(t)\ne w(t+1),\qquad m_e(w)\equiv0\pmod 2\quad\text{for every }e.w(t)=w(t+1),me​(w)≡0(mod2)for every e.

All indexing sets are finite, so Lean can decide this predicate by finite computation.The subtype DoubleCoveredClosedWalk packages a cyclic walk together with this property.

Write En=E∥M∥E_n=\mathbb E\lVert M\rVertEn​=E∥M∥ for the expected operator norm.For a moment order kkk, write Tn,k=Etr⁡(M2k)T_{n,k}=\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(M^{2k})Tn,k​=Etr(M2k).

Analytic input

Norm from trace moments

Lemma 1

Even trace moments control the mean norm

Let k≥1k\ge1k≥1 and B≥0B\ge0B≥0.If Tn,k≤B2kT_{n,k}\le B^{2k}Tn,k​≤B2k, then En≤BE_n\le BEn​≤B.
Etr⁡(M2k)≤B2k⟹E∥M∥≤B.\mathbb E\operatorname{tr}(M^{2k})\le B^{2k}\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\mathbb E\lVert M\rVert\le B.Etr(M2k)≤B2k⟹E∥M∥≤B.
Proof sketch.Indeed, symmetry gives ∥M∥2k≤tr⁡(M2k)\lVert M\rVert^{2k}\le\operatorname{tr}(M^{2k})∥M∥2k≤tr(M2k), and the power-mean inequality gives (E∥M∥)2k≤E∥M∥2k(\mathbb E\lVert M\rVert)^{2k}\le\mathbb E\lVert M\rVert^{2k}(E∥M∥)2k≤E∥M∥2k.The Lean proof is intentionally left as sorry.
03
Combinatorial input

Trace as a walk count

Lemma 2

Exact trace expansion

For k≥1k\ge1k≥1, the expected trace power is exactly the number of double-covered closed walks of length 2k2k2k.
Tn,k=#Wn,2keven.T_{n,k}=\#\mathcal W^{\mathrm{even}}_{n,2k}.Tn,k​=#Wn,2keven​.
Proof sketch.Expanding the trace produces one monomial for each cyclic vertex sequence.A stationary step contributes zero because the matrix diagonal vanishes.For a loopless walk, independence and centering make the expected monomial zero unless every edge occurs an even number of times; in that case it equals one.The Lean proof is left as sorry.
Lemma 3

A crude pairing bound

For k≥1k\ge1k≥1, the surviving walks satisfy
#Wn,2keven≤n(n−1)nk−1(4k)k.\#\mathcal W^{\mathrm{even}}_{n,2k}\le n(n-1)n^{k-1}(4k)^k.#Wn,2keven​≤n(n−1)nk−1(4k)k.
Proof sketch.Pair the occurrences of each edge.There are at most (2k)k(2k)^k(2k)k pairings and at most 2k2^k2k orientation choices.The used graph is connected and has at most kkk edges, hence at most k+1k+1k+1 vertices.Choosing the first distinct pair and the remaining vertex labels gives the displayed bound.The Lean proof is left as sorry.
04
Choice of moment

Pay only a square root of a logarithm

Lemma 4

Logarithmic optimization

Set k=⌊log⁡2n⌋+1k=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1k=⌊log2​n⌋+1, written in Lean as Nat.log 2 n + 1.Then the crude count is bounded by the 2k2k2k-th power of 8nlog⁡n8\sqrt n\sqrt{\log n}8n​logn​.
n(n−1)nk−1(4k)k≤(8nlog⁡n)2k.n(n-1)n^{k-1}(4k)^k\le\bigl(8\sqrt n\sqrt{\log n}\bigr)^{2k}.n(n−1)nk−1(4k)k≤(8n​logn​)2k.
Proof sketch.This is elementary arithmetic: taking a 2k2k2k-th root turns (4k)k(4k)^k(4k)k into 2k2\sqrt k2k​, while the choice of kkk keeps n1/(2k)n^{1/(2k)}n1/(2k) bounded.For n≤1n\le1n≤1, the factor n(n−1)n(n-1)n(n−1) makes the estimate immediate.The generous constant eight absorbs the change from binary to natural logarithms and the small dimensions.The Lean proof is left as sorry.
05
Conclusion

The expected norm bound

Main theorem
There is a universal constant C>0C>0C>0 such that, for every nnn,
E∥M∥≤Cnlog⁡n.\mathbb E\lVert M\rVert\le C\sqrt n\sqrt{\log n}.E∥M∥≤Cn​logn​.
Proof from the lemmas
  1. 1Take C=8C=8C=8 and k=⌊log⁡2n⌋+1k=\lfloor\log_2 n\rfloor+1k=⌊log2​n⌋+1; this moment order is positive.
  2. 2Apply Lemma 1 with B=8nlog⁡nB=8\sqrt n\sqrt{\log n}B=8n​logn​; it remains to bound Tn,kT_{n,k}Tn,k​ by B2kB^{2k}B2k.
  3. 3Lemma 2 identifies Tn,kT_{n,k}Tn,k​ with #Wn,2keven\#\mathcal W^{\mathrm{even}}_{n,2k}#Wn,2keven​.
  4. 4Lemma 3 bounds this cardinality by n(n−1)nk−1(4k)kn(n-1)n^{k-1}(4k)^kn(n−1)nk−1(4k)k.
  5. 5Lemma 4 bounds the latter quantity by B2kB^{2k}B2k, completing the proof.
